item.title: Re: Incorporeal mass at the center of the Earth
item.content:encoded:
How does the computer communicate from the center of the earth? I honestly can't imagine just handwaving this sorta thing… how does a signal travel from an incorporeal electronic device to physical electronic devices, through miles and miles of solid mass?

It's a Foundation long-distance communicator utilizing anomalous tech. Given that the Foundation has communication methods that can communicate extra-dimensionally and that most types of communication are intangible anyway, I don't feel communicating with an intangible computer is much of a stretch. And Foundation technology pretty much renders distance and matter separations irrelevant.

Why are there so many bodies down there? Like what is happening to make this occur? I can't imagine people are being turned incorporeal this often… If they are, why isn't that the SCP and not the bodies at the center of the earth?

The anomaly is the collection of everyone who has ever become intangible and fallen through the floor and it has been building up over many thousands of years. The bodies come from as far-flung sources as ancient trickster gods, experimental para-technology from an Occult war and quite a few from previous iterations of SCP-2000. Lastly while most bodies are dead, none have decomposed due to their intangible nature. As for some central object or entity causing this, that's simply not the case. This isn't a sinister plot or experiment gone wrong, this is an inevitability in a world with intangibility.

+ show block
– hide block

If the agents are deaf, dumb and blind (I don't know why because the post doesn't say, but I assume because of their status deep in the earth)… how can they tell the Foundation anything? They have no sensation (because tactile is out, due to their incorporeality).

I still think there isn't much to this narrative. It feels like a description of people suffering… but what is the arc here? Just "we're intangible, and at the center of the earth!" and then dying? (Also how would the agents even know about that they're in the center of the earth?)

Good point. I have changed the original post to explain how the agents understand and can interact with their situation.

Which is that they don't.

To the agents, they have been plunged into complete darkness, unable to move or touch anything, with a faint sensation of things (the other intangible people) filling the same space as them. To the agent with the computer, the computer is an outlet through by which they can call for help and via which may one day be rescued. So they desperately type at the computer, relying solely on muscle memory, not knowing whether what they are typing is being revived and unable to know if anyone has replied. The narrative is the story of that agents' experience, how they go from fearing, to hopeful, to desperate, and the implication that many other people have gone through that experience without the chance of salvation and will continue doing so indefinitely. It's a description of people suffering, but the story of one of those people shows how hopeless, prolonged and empty that suffering is.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: Re: Incorporeal mass at the center of the Earth
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for the feedback. I will try and clarify a few things:

+ Clarifications
- Close

Why is this happening?

Because over the years many people have became intangible and fallen to the center of the earth.

Why is the majority of objects at the center “human corpses”?

Because humans are the most common thing to turn intangible and fall through the fall due to our natural desire for power, in this case, the power to walk through walls. Naturally there are also other animals and inanimate objects in there as well.

How is it possible that they number in the billions?

This anomaly has been building up over many thousands of years. The bodies come from as far-flung sources as ancient trickster gods, experimental para-technology from an Occult war and quite a few from previous iterations of SCP-2000. Lastly while most bodies are dead, none have decomposed due to their intangible nature.

Why are the agents “blind, deaf and mute”? If so, how do they even use a computer?

The agents are "blind, deaf and mute" due to how their eyes ears and mouths are located entirely within the solid matter of the earth inner core. They use a computer because it was in contact with one of them when they became intangible, staying intangible as well and allowing the intangible agent to use it.

Similarly, why does the effect suddenly wear off and they die?

Because all types of intangibly eventually wear off after a certain amount of time within a solid or liquid. They agents die when they become tangible enough to suffocate.

Lastly, the Foundation not pursuing containment of the anomaly is not in line with their motto.

The Foundation isn't containing it because:
1. It's effectively self-containing due to it's location.
2. There is not feasible way to remove it from it's location.
3. The threat to exposure to the public is extremely small.
4. If they were somehow able to remove it, it would inevitably end up there again upon the first containment breach.

Basically, the MTF goes incorporeal, communicate with the Foundation, and then they die? You need more than that, especially if you want to give your readers some semblance of answers as to what’s going on.

The narrative of the article is the story of that MTF and their gradual transformation from hopeful, to weary to despairing and begging for rescue. At first they help the foundation in any way they can by communicating with them an informing them of the anomaly and trying to help them document it. After a while they realize they won't be rescued. As for answers, there are none. This isn't a sinister plot or experiment gone wrong, this is an inevitability in a world with intangibility.

Other suggestions might be to explain the origins of the anomaly, how/why the CI is involved and how exactly the Foundation goes about trying to contain this.

1. The anomaly is the collection of everyone who has ever become intangible and fallen through the floor.
2. The CI is a plot device explaining how an entire MTF was turned intangible. They have little importance to the anomaly overall. The CI could be change to the SH or an experiment gone wrong.
3. The Foundation can't/won't/doesn't need to contain the anomaly due to it's nature, being content with observation and documentation.

Hope this clears up few things up!

item.title: Re: Incorporeal mass at the center of the Earth

Summoned via PM:

Hi there Undercover Fly. Let’s take a look at your concept.

I see that you’ve revised the article a few times based on the other reviewers’ feedback. Unfortunately, my concerns boil down to two that I hope you can expand on / clarify:

1) Plot inconsistencies / lack of clarity. Why is this happening? It’s never hinted at / explained in your pitch besides mention of the Chaos Insurgency. More importantly, why is the majority of objects at the center “human corpses”, and how is it possible that they number in the billions? Just what exactly is happening? Why are the agents “blind, deaf and mute”? If so, how do they even use a computer? Similarly, why does the effect suddenly wear off and they die? Lastly, the Foundation not pursuing containment of the anomaly is not in line with their motto.

2) There still isn’t a coherent / developed narrative. The only line I can glimpse from your Central Narrative portion is an exploration log? Basically, the MTF goes incorporeal, communicate with the Foundation, and then they die? You need more than that, especially if you want to give your readers some semblance of answers as to what’s going on. Other suggestions might be to explain the origins of the anomaly, how/why the CI is involved and how exactly the Foundation goes about trying to contain this.

If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll take another look. Best of luck!

item.title: Re: Incorporeal mass at the center of the Earth
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for the feedback. Some responses below.

+ Collapsed for brevity
- Close

If something was incorporeal in the core and then became corporeal, why would the core collapse?

It isn't simply more mass being added to the core, it is part of the core being replaced with the incorporeal objects, which are far less dense, allowing large amounts of additional matter to be pushed into the core in a large surge. it should also be noted that due to the nature of several types of intangibility there are several intangible corpse in a single place being expelled from each other while becoming corporeal, potentially causing large seismic disruptions due to the movement of large amounts of mass. As for the 'disastrous' aspect, that is what is being implied to happen in the scenario discussed at the end.

Don't do this, don't redact the size. It doesn't serve anything, do some research and figure out what sorta size you want to imply and just say it. Would be more impactful.

Fair enough, but what more impact would a unit of measure have? I am of the opinion that a well placed redaction can emphasize the horror of an article. To anyone who isn't familiar with the size of a human body or the size of the earths core a definitive amount I feel a definitive amount would lessen the impact. That being said, I may just blackbox the exact volume with a large amount of digits.

More of concern is the lack of narrative. There isn't an arc to this, its merely discussing the description of an anomaly. What is it you want to say with this article? What do you want the readers to take away from it? We can't really know what the people are going through as they sink to the center of the earth… so where is the human aspect of this anomaly?

You are correct in there not being a central narrative but for an anomaly of this type, there can't really be one, as it isn't the result of one central anomaly. The human aspect of this article comes in the form of the individual stories of the people down there, implied through their descriptions. Furthermore, due to the nature of certain types of intangibility some of the people are still alive and fully aware of their situation. Given that I am planning on having at least one of the people as a ghost, the foundation may be able to conduct an interview with them via use of a séance. Ending the article with the potential of disaster is meant to convey how this is truly a lose-lose situation, with them being stuck, us being doomed and neither party being able to do anything about it.

EDIT: Upon further consideration I have decided to add a central narrative regarding a group of foundation researchers and soldiers trapped in this mass and acting as a sort of 'rescue group' for other living people in the mass. This group is how the foundation first learns of the anomaly and have developed a unique system of communication by touch given that they are all essentially all blind, deaf and mute.

item.title: Re: Incorporeal mass at the center of the Earth
item.content:encoded:
Here are some minor quibbles with the internal logic you've presented:

+ show block
– hide block

causing part of it to become corporal before the unit is destroyed, causing part of the earths core to collapse in on itself, creating a minor earthquake.

Several things with this: a) If something was incorporeal in the core and then became corporeal, why would the core collapse? The core isn't hollow, its solid with liquified rock. Also, the core is made the way it is because of gravity pushing innumerable metric tons of matter into it, I can't imagine a little more would suddenly make it collapse even a teensy bit. More than likely that matter would then be vaporized by the intense heat and then some small amount of gas would escape the core potentially (but this is happening all the time). b) if part of the core were to collapse it wouldn't make a "minor earthquake" it would probably be disastrous.

The exact size of this mass is [REDACTED] by it is implied to be truly massive.

Don't do this, don't redact the size. It doesn't serve anything, do some research and figure out what sorta size you want to imply and just say it. Would be more impactful. Also in general, I am of the opinion that "redacted" information doesn't serve narratives in 99% of the case. Here isn't an exception to me.

More of concern is the lack of narrative. There isn't an arc to this, its merely discussing the description of an anomaly. What is it you want to say with this article? What do you want the readers to take away from it? We can't really know what the people are going through as they sink to the center of the earth… so where is the human aspect of this anomaly?

I think you should brainstorm concerning a narrative. Think about what sort of story you want to tell and come up with a way to tell it with this anomaly. Because at the end of the day, most articles that only concern themselves with "look at this weird phenomenon" don't do well. If you have some clever way to avoid using narrative to getting the reader engaged, I am not seeing it.

item.title: Re: Incorporeal mass at the center of the Earth
item.content:encoded: I like the suggestion of using neutrinos, as they seem to be the closest real-world equivalent to 'incorporeal energy'. As for the fading intangibility I am considering a concept of 'neutrino diffusion', similar to 'hume diffusion' in SCP-3001 and SCP-4903, wherein the intangibility is slowly being shared between the incorporeal objects and earths inner core. This would lead to a sudden absence of the inner core, causing a much more disastrous collapse than would happen if the inner core were replaced with corpses. This would also solve the debate of whether the re-materializing object would replace the solid matter or the other way round. What do you think?

item.title: Incorporeal mass at the center of the Earth
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP format with the containment procedures, description, incident log and a log of several SCP-XXXX instances (Possibly collaborative).

Elevator Pitch: Incorporeality is a a common power of anomalies. In most cases this is accompanied by some form of levitation. But happened to all those people who have accomplished the former, but not the latter?

Central Narrative: The SCP is a group of incorporeal objects located at the center of the earth, the majority of which are human corpses. All of these corpses are located at a single point, the gravitational center of the earth, with there being a staggering amount of bodies, over a billion. It is in fact the resting place of every person who has became incorporeal and fallen through the ground. The way that the foundation learned about this anomaly is that a group of foundation researchers and soldiers got trapped in the mass after being turn incorporeal by the CI during an attack. Transmissions received from this group allowed the foundation to locate and document it and their communication with them emphasizes how horrible it is in there. Analysis reveals many of the people in the core are still alive and unable to change their situation. Given that the agents are all essentially blind, deaf and mute due to them being entirely encased in solid matter, they communicate with the foundation through an incorporeal computer that fell with them, which utilizes anomalous communication technology. On behalf of the foundation they attempt to document their experience (as they are unaware of the nature of their situation) and eventually figure out a way escape from it, but can't. Foundation attempts at response are constantly thwarted due to the person not being able to see them or know that they have been received. They lose contact with the foundation when it is revealed that their form of intangibility used on them wares off, leaving them to be crushed by the intense pressure. The last communication is a call for help, begging for rescue, not only for them but for any other people trapped like they are. A note at the end describes how the foundation isn't pursuing this avenue of research due to logistics and a lack of benefits.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Taking a semi-used joke to its logical conclusion.

Additional Notes: In this article 'intangibility' also extends to 'partial immunity from outside stimuli' explaining why many of the people in the core are still alive. The ones that are dead are the ones who's intangibility wore off slowly enough that they starved, dehydrated, overheated or died form the pressure. Others died of old age.
